newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO warns Israeli Arabs against land sale to Jews.
newsitem.headline: PLO warns Israeli Arabs against land sale to Jews.

text.p: Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen warned Arabs with Israeli citizenship on Tuesday they too could face the death penalty if caught selling land to Jews.
Abu Medeen announced earlier this month, citing an old Jordanian law, that Palestinians could be executed for selling land to Jews.
"Last month the Palestinian Authority took a decision to forbid and prohibit the sale of Palestinian land to Israelis," Abu Medeen told a news conference.
"I warn and advise those Palestinians who have become Israeli citizens that this will not protect them. They will be tried in one way or another," he said.
The PLO has said the ban was necessary to halt the expansion of Jewish settlements in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Arab East Jerusalem, occupied by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
Palestinians see settlements as an Israeli attempt to thwart their goal of founding an independent state in the areas.
The Palestinian Authority controls parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under a 1993 self-rule deal with Israel. PLO police are limited to operating solely in the areas under Palestinian rule.
Israel has called the ban "racist" and linked it with the recent killings of two Palestinian land dealers found dead in the West Bank. The PLO denies the charges.
One of the two land dealers found dead in PLO-ruled Ramallah, 70 year-old Farid Bashiti, was an Israeli citizen.
"The Palestinian Authority is not involved in the killings that took place. Maybe the Israelis did it for blackmail or maybe normal people did it," Abu Medeen said.
The United States last week strongly criticised Palestinian President Yasser Arafat after an Israeli newspaper quoted him as backing the decision to enforce the death penalty.
Abu Medeen said the PLO was interrogating "seven to 12" Palestinians on suspicion of selling land to Israelis.
